# Introduction {#sec-introduction} ## Data sources | Source | Access | Used for | |--------|--------|----------| | OCR catalogue extraction | Notebook and CSV outputs from the linked-open-exhibition pipeline | Structured artwork metadata extracted from scanned catalogue pages | | CPS Wikibase | SPARQL, `https://cps.tibwiki.io/query/proxy/sparql` | Works, materials, persons, exhibition, catalogue | | Wikidata | SPARQL, `https://query.wikidata.org/sparql` | Context about the artist and linked entities | | DNB | SRU, `https://services.dnb.de/sru/dnb` (MARC21-xml) | Publications by and about the artist | All queries are stored as `.rq` files in `src/baldessari/queries/` or as strings in the Python package `baldessari`, so they can be reused outside the book. ## Data model of the CPS Wikibase Each CPS item has one or more *types* (property P3). An item can carry several types at once: a work may be both an *artwork* and a *painting*. The figures below therefore count items per type and do not add up to the total number of items. ::: {#tbl-types .cell tbl-cap='Number of CPS items per type.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

The CPS data describe a catalogue of works together with the materials and persons needed to describe them. ## Catalogue used as a source Much of the data was derived from the exhibition catalogue @baldessari1999 through OCR-assisted extraction and curation. The catalogue is itself an item in the CPS Wikibase and is linked to the DNB (see [Chapter -@sec-dnb]).
